Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old man with known asthma presents via telehealth with 3 hours of chest tightness, wheeze, and mild exertional dyspnea after a recent URI; assessment consistent with an acute asthma exacerbation likely viral-triggered and worsened by a lapse in inhaler use. Management: SABA and ICS refills, 5-day oral steroids, spacer, safety-net advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Chest tightness x ~3 hours; mild shortness of breath (not at rest), worse with exertion (stairs); wheeze; non-productive cough. Recent cold last week (sore throat, runny nose) with persistent cough; cough slightly worse at night. Tightness rather than pain; sensation of not getting a full breath.
- Associated symptoms: Recent URI features as above; denies productive sputum; denies rest dyspnea; denies chest pain.
- Past medical history: Asthma since childhood; severe exacerbation requiring intubation at ~16–17 years. Allergic rhinitis/hay fever; dust allergy. Childhood eczema and milk protein allergy.
- Medications: Previously salbutamol (Ventolin) PRN and beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) maintenance; ran out ~1 week ago and has not used either since.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Mother—eczema; father—asthma.
- Social/preventive: University student. Tobacco/alcohol/drug use not discussed.

Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals or physical exam recorded.
- Patient not short of breath at rest; able to speak in full sentences. No peak flow available.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation, likely triggered by recent viral URI and exacerbated by one week without controller/reliever inhalers.
  - Supporting: Known asthma with atopy; recent URI; current wheeze, chest tightness, exertional dyspnea; non-productive cough; medication lapse.
- Differential (lower likelihood):
  - Post-viral bronchial hyperreactivity/acute viral bronchitis: Persistent cough after URI may contribute.
  - Community-acquired pneumonia: Low—no fever, sputum, or pleuritic pain.
  - Pulmonary embolism or spontaneous pneumothorax: Low—no risk factors or typical features reported.

Plan:
- Medications:
  - Re-prescribe salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler PRN.
  - Re-prescribe beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) maintenance inhaler; resume as maintenance once improved (morning use discussed).
  - Start short course of oral steroids: tablets for 5 days, 2 tablets each morning.
  - Provide spacer device; usage instructions reviewed.
- Counseling/safety net:
  - Steroid side effects discussed: possible mood changes, increased blood sugar, rash, nausea, headache; advised to read medication information.
  - Seek medical care if needing salbutamol more often than every 3 hours.
  - Red flags: worsening shortness of breath, increasing chest tightness/pain, light-headedness—seek urgent care.
- Logistics:
  - Prescriptions to be sent within the hour.
  - Rest advised; may self-certify off work for up to 7 days.
- Follow-up:
  - No specific follow-up arranged; advised to seek medical attention if symptoms persist or deteriorate.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals and objective measures (O2 saturation, peak flow), smoking status, exact oral steroid name/strength/dose, in-person inhaler technique review, explicit follow-up appointment, vaccination status (influenza/COVID), recent exacerbation frequency.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor audio dropouts; no objective exam due to telehealth limitations.
